plan.planning_summary: This portfolio tests three distinct physical approaches to achieving dual-band spectral performance (high UV reflection, high SWIR transmission) within a 30-layer HfO2/SiO2 constraint on fused silica. Route 1 tests whether a classic periodic quarter-wave Bragg stack centered on the UV band can achieve sufficient SWIR transmission as a baseline. Route 2 tests whether chirping layer thicknesses through the stack broadens the UV reflection band without degrading SWIR transmission. Route 3 tests whether introducing a defect cavity layer creates a transmission resonance in the SWIR band while maintaining UV reflection. These axes are genuinely distinct: periodic vs. graded vs. cavity-enhanced topologies explore different interference mechanisms. Literature L01 and L03 support the HfO2/SiO2 material system choice; L02 supports the optimization approach; L22 supports dichroic design principles. No route claims validation from literature - all performance is determined by the solver.

routes.title: Periodic Quarter-Wave Bragg Stack for UV Reflection
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic quarter-wave Bragg stack centered at 375 nm (mid-UV band) using HfO2/SiO2 pairs will achieve high reflection in 300-450 nm while maintaining adequate transmission in 1000-1700 nm due to the natural transparency of dielectric stacks outside their stopband.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave optical thickness layers at the center wavelength of the reflection band create constructive interference for reflection. Outside the stopband, the stack becomes increasingly transparent as wavelength increases, potentially allowing SWIR transmission.
routes.proposed_topology: air / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / sio2_substrate
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 20 coating layers
soft_objectives: minimize layer count while meeting spectral targets
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 are standard ion-beam sputtering materials
quarter-wave thicknesses at 375 nm are approximately 50-70 nm per layer, manufacturable
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
expected_advantages: Low layer count leaves margin for optimization
known_risks: May not achieve sufficient SWIR transmission if stopband extends too far
UV reflection bandwidth may be narrower than 300-450 nm requirement
Angle sensitivity not characterized
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 20-layer periodic dielectric coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: air / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / SiO2 (Lemarchand)_substrate. Optimize all 20 layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and maximize reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Use only hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) materials. Maximum 30 layers constraint satisfied with 20 layers.

routes.title: Chirped Thickness Stack for Broadband UV Reflection
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A chirped stack with progressively varying layer optical thicknesses will broaden the UV reflection band (300-450 nm) compared to a periodic stack, while maintaining SWIR transmission through careful thickness progression design.
routes.design_principle: Varying layer thicknesses through the stack creates multiple overlapping reflection bands at different wavelengths, effectively broadening the total reflection bandwidth. Thinner layers reflect shorter wavelengths, thicker layers reflect longer wavelengths within the UV band.
routes.proposed_topology: air / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / sio2_substrate

soft_objectives: maximize mean reflectance across full 300-450 nm band
achieve smooth thickness progression to support manufacturability
manufacturing_considerations: Chirped designs require precise thickness control but are manufacturable with modern deposition systems
Thickness variation should be monotonic to support process control
theory_basis: Multiple resonance overlap for bandwidth broadening
expected_advantages: Broader UV reflection band than periodic stack
known_risks: More complex optimization landscape than periodic stack
May require more iterations to converge
Thickness progression constraint may limit optimal solutions

Stack sequence: air / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / SiO2 (Lemarchand)_substrate. Optimize all 24 layer thicknesses with a chirp progression (thickness varies systematically through stack depth) to maximize reflectance in 300-450 nm band and transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band. Use only hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) materials. Maximum 30 layers constraint satisfied with 24 layers.

routes.title: Defect-Cavity Bandpass Stack for Enhanced SWIR Transmission
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Introducing a half-wave defect cavity layer in the center of a Bragg stack will create a transmission resonance in the SWIR band (1000-1700 nm) while the surrounding Bragg mirrors maintain high UV reflection (300-450 nm).
routes.design_principle: A defect layer in a photonic bandgap structure creates a localized transmission state within the stopband. By placing the cavity resonance in the SWIR band and designing the mirrors for UV reflection, dual-band performance can be achieved through spatial separation of spectral functions.
routes.proposed_topology: air / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / sio2_substrate
soft_objectives: maximize transmittance peak in 1000-1700 nm band
minimize sideband transmission outside target bands
manufacturing_considerations: Cavity layer requires precise thickness control for resonance positioning
Symmetric mirror design simplifies deposition sequencing
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot cavity resonance in multilayer stacks
expected_advantages: Sharper transmission band in SWIR than broadband approaches
Better spectral selectivity for methane detection band
Mirror sections can be optimized independently for UV reflection
known_risks: Transmission band may be narrower than 1000-1700 nm requirement
Cavity resonance sensitive to thickness errors
May require more layers to achieve sufficient UV reflection with cavity insertion
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 21-layer defect-cavity dielectric coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: air / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / hfo2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / SiO2 (Lemarchand)_substrate with layer 11 (hfo2) serving as the central cavity. Optimize 18 mirror layer thicknesses and 1 cavity layer thickness to create a transmission resonance in 1000-1700 nm band while maintaining high reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Use only hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) materials. Maximum 30 layers constraint satisfied with 21 layers.

routes.title: Quarter-wave UV-rejection dichroic stack on fused silica
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave stack centered at 375 nm will produce reflectance >80% in the 300-450 nm band while maintaining transmittance >85% in the 1000-1700 nm band, with performance improving monotonically as layer thicknesses approach the quarter-wave condition.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create photonic bandgaps at the design wavelength. A UV-centered stack naturally transmits longer wavelengths where the optical thickness becomes sub-quarter-wave. High-low index contrast (HfO2 ~2.0, SiO2 ~1.45) determines stopband width and peak reflectance.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (24 layers total, 12 pairs, starting with HfO2 from air side)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers, tuned around quarter-wave optical thickness at 375 nm center wavelength
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 24 (under 30-layer limit)
Individual layer thicknesses must be manufacturable (typically >20 nm for uniformity)
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard evaporatable/sputterable dielectrics
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stacks produce maximum reflectance when each layer has optical thickness = λ0/4 at the design wavelength
Starting with high-index layer from low-index incidence medium (air) improves first-surface reflection contribution
Stopband width scales with index contrast ratio nH/nL
Transmission bands appear at wavelengths where optical thickness becomes integer multiples of half-wavelength
More layer pairs increase peak reflectance and stopband width but add complexity
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology is well-understood and manufacturable
24 layers provides good UV rejection while staying under 30-layer limit
HfO2/SiO2 pair offers high index contrast for wide stopband
Quarter-wave design naturally passes SWIR band without additional optimization
known_risks: Refractive index values recalled approximately: HfO2 ~1.9-2.1, SiO2 ~1.45-1.48 in visible/NIR - actual dispersion data from material_catalog must be used
Quarter-wave thickness calculation depends on exact n(λ) at 375 nm which I am recalling, not looking up - physical thickness = λ0/(4×n) needs verified n values
Angle of incidence not specified in request - I assume normal incidence (0°) as a hypothesis; oblique incidence would shift band edges
Polarization not specified - I assume unpolarized light; TE/TM split at non-zero angle could affect performance
Extinction coefficients in UV band uncertain - HfO2 may have some absorption below 350 nm that I cannot confirm without data
What would settle these: material_catalog n/k dispersion curves for hfo2 and sio2 across 300-1700 nm, verified by the local registry
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 24-layer periodic dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence from air side: HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), then fused silica substrate. Optimize individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers. Wavelength bands: maximize reflectance in 300-450 nm, maximize transmittance in 1000-1700 nm. Incidence angle: 0 degrees (normal). Polarization: unpolarized (average of TE and TM). Materials: hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) only. Maximum layer count: 24 (fixed). Use material_catalog dispersion data for hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand).

research_influence: L01 (HfO2/SiO2 nanolaminates) informed the material pair selection for all three routes, confirming HfO2 and SiO2 as a viable high-index/low-index pair for dielectric stacks
L02 (global optimization for thin-film systems) informed the optimization strategy declaration in all routes, supporting the use of deterministic optimization for finding global solutions
L03 (HfO2-SiO2 optical constants) supported the material property assumptions for the HfO2/SiO2 system in the design principles
L08 (manufacture of complex multilayer filters) informed manufacturing considerations regarding layer count feasibility and deposition control
L22 (dichroic beam combiner coating) informed the defect-cavity route design principle, as it demonstrates dual-band spectral separation in dielectric stacks
unresolved_decisions: Incidence angle not specified in original request - all routes assume normal incidence (0 degrees) as baseline, but angle sensitivity should be evaluated in post-optimization analysis

Polarization state not specified - all routes assume unpolarized or average of s and p polarization, but polarization-dependent performance may need characterization for off-axis rays in the camera system
Fused silica substrate refractive index dispersion not explicitly provided - using sio2 catalog entry which should resolve to fused silica dataset
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all three routes fail to achieve best_target_score above 0.5 after full optimization iterations, reconsider whether the 30-layer constraint is too restrictive for the dual-band requirement, or whether additional material options beyond HfO2/SiO2 are needed. Do not relax wavelength band requirements as they are driven by the methane detection application.

errors: This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone. No Semantic Scholar query was issued, no retrieved paper reached the prompt, and no method-research report was supplied -- neither for the initial plan nor for any continuation round. It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against the literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests a quarter-wave dielectric stack design centered on the UV rejection band (300-450 nm), using recalled thin-film optics principles. The hypothesis is that a HfO2/SiO2 periodic stack with optical thicknesses tuned to ~375 nm center wavelength will create a high-reflectance stopband in UV while naturally transmitting the SWIR band (1000-1700 nm). This route uses no retrieved literature - all design choices come from the model's prior knowledge of dichroic filter design patterns.

routes.title: Quarter-wave UV-rejection dichroic stack on fused silica
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave stack centered at 375 nm will produce reflectance >80% in the 300-450 nm band while maintaining transmittance >85% in the 1000-1700 nm band, with performance improving monotonically as layer thicknesses approach the quarter-wave condition.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create photonic bandgaps at the design wavelength. A UV-centered stack naturally transmits longer wavelengths where the optical thickness becomes sub-quarter-wave. High-low index contrast (HfO2 ~2.0, SiO2 ~1.45) determines stopband width and peak reflectance.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (24 layers total, 12 pairs, starting with HfO2 from air side)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers, tuned around quarter-wave optical thickness at 375 nm center wavelength
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 24 (under 30-layer limit)
Individual layer thicknesses must be manufacturable (typically >20 nm for uniformity)
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard evaporatable/sputterable dielectrics
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stacks produce maximum reflectance when each layer has optical thickness = λ0/4 at the design wavelength
Starting with high-index layer from low-index incidence medium (air) improves first-surface reflection contribution
Stopband width scales with index contrast ratio nH/nL
Transmission bands appear at wavelengths where optical thickness becomes integer multiples of half-wavelength
More layer pairs increase peak reflectance and stopband width but add complexity
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology is well-understood and manufacturable
24 layers provides good UV rejection while staying under 30-layer limit
HfO2/SiO2 pair offers high index contrast for wide stopband
Quarter-wave design naturally passes SWIR band without additional optimization
known_risks: Refractive index values recalled approximately: HfO2 ~1.9-2.1, SiO2 ~1.45-1.48 in visible/NIR - actual dispersion data from material_catalog must be used
Quarter-wave thickness calculation depends on exact n(λ) at 375 nm which I am recalling, not looking up - physical thickness = λ0/(4×n) needs verified n values
Angle of incidence not specified in request - I assume normal incidence (0°) as a hypothesis; oblique incidence would shift band edges
Polarization not specified - I assume unpolarized light; TE/TM split at non-zero angle could affect performance
Extinction coefficients in UV band uncertain - HfO2 may have some absorption below 350 nm that I cannot confirm without data
What would settle these: material_catalog n/k dispersion curves for hfo2 and sio2 across 300-1700 nm, verified by the local registry
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 24-layer periodic dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence from air side: HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), then fused silica substrate. Optimize individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers. Wavelength bands: maximize reflectance in 300-450 nm, maximize transmittance in 1000-1700 nm. Incidence angle: 0 degrees (normal). Polarization: unpolarized (average of TE and TM). Materials: hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) only. Maximum layer count: 24 (fixed). Use material_catalog dispersion data for hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand).
